account: It is day 1 at six in the morning, and I have just woken at home. I have seen nothing unusual this morning. Yesterday the neighbour described the riverside as peaceful, with no request for town hall, and passed on the baker's announcement of fresh bread. The secretary reported no new correspondence or afternoon business. Someone identified as freight appeared at town hall, but I did not hear any business from them, so I do not know their purpose. Today's recorded routine includes office hours at eight, a grain inspection at the east-bank mill at ten, lunch at home at noon, council letters at thirteen, tea with the neighbour at fifteen, and office hours at sixteen thirty. The addition to the usual schedule is the innkeeper's confirmed meeting: they will meet me at my office at seventeen forty-five and accompany me to the great hall for eighteen to discuss the inn's service to town. I have no evidence of another purpose for that meeting. I should read the appointment book again this morning and keep these appointments.
